name: Ischemic Stroke Urine SERS, 532 nm laser (Yu et al. 2026)
description: Surface-enhanced Raman (SERS) spectra of urine from 101 participants (55 healthy controls, 46 patients with confirmed ischemic stroke) on colloidal Ag-nanoparticle SERS filter-paper chips (R6G enhancement factor 1.62e6), Renishaw inVia Qontor, 50x objective, 1 s acquisition, 532 nm excitation (100 mW (0.5% power setting)). Each participant's dried urine spot was scanned as a 10x10 map (100 spectra); the deposit additionally contains four repeated collections (files 31.1-34.1), so each variant holds 10,500 spectra from 105 map files (the paper's headline 10,100 counts only the 101 primary maps). Native WiRE axes (667-668 points at 532 nm, 1,015 points at 633 nm; ~485-1,638 cm^-1; slightly non-uniform) resampled row-wise onto a common 1 cm^-1 grid (1,154 points). group_ids = the 101 participants (repeat collections merged into the parent participant), so all spectra of one group share one class. Raw WiRE exports as deposited: the authors' baseline correction, smoothing, normalization, and outlier removal (which dropped ~8% of the map points, incl. all-zero scans) live in their analysis code/results, not in the deposited spectra.
